verdict.reasoning: Patient reports fever for about seven days with alternating hot and cold sensations, night sweats, myalgias, nausea, decreased appetite, low fluid intake, and fatigue: "I've been struggling with fever for the past week. Yeah, I would say it started about seven days ago... I'm really hot and sweaty all the time... I'd say that I'm aching all over, really. My muscles are really aching. I'm feeling quite nauseous, so I've not been able to eat very much and I have been drinking, but it's been quite a small amount. Just generally quite tired and unwell. I'm sweating during the night. I'm quite cold."

Patient denies cough/cold/sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, rash, and joint problems: "Not those sort of symptoms really" regarding cough/cold/sore throat; "No, my ears are fine"; "Have you had any diarrhea? Patient: Not. Not really, no. I'm fine"; "Have you got any neck stiffness at all? Patient: No"; "Have you got any rash in your body anywhere at all? Patient: I haven't noticed any rashes, no"; "Any joints swollen or tender or sore? Patient: Not really. I mean, I often have problems with back pain, but not really any other joints?" Joint swelling/tenderness elsewhere is denied. Coryza is not explicitly mentioned but grouped under “cough or cold” is a reasonable inference.

Headaches are described as baseline, central, screen/weather-related, not worse than usual, with history of migraines: "Do you have any headache? Patient: Not more than usual, no. Just like the general headaches, but not just from staring at the screen. No migraines or anything." and "It's quite centralized over the head." and "It's something that I've struggled with for years, really, just related to screen use or like changes in weather patterns, high pressure days. Sometimes I struggle with migraines and headaches."

Travel to Vietnam 4 weeks ago with rural and urban exposure including trekking/cycling through farmland is documented: "Patient: I went to Vietnam. I came back four weeks ago now" and "we toured to several different parts of the country in the countryside and some cities as well" and "We were sort of trekking and cycling through farmland."

Patient took daily malaria prophylaxis, doesn’t recall name, and thinks there was a second tablet: "Doctor: did you take malaria preventative medication..." "Patient: I did, yes"; "Doctor: Was it a weekly tablet or a daily tablet? Patient: I think it was daily"; "Doctor: ...was there another one that you would take on top of the first one? Patient: I think it was another one that I took on top of the first one." Name is indeed unknown.

Chronic postural back pain and current physiotherapy are described: "I often have problems with back pain" and later "As I said, I've been struggling with back pain for quite a while" and "I'm under a physiotherapist at the moment for that" and "They've said that it's related to long periods of time sitting at a desk and just bad posture."
Patient is taking ibuprofen: "I've been trying to like take ibuprofen and paracetamol just from over the counter."
Patient is taking paracetamol: "I've been trying to like take ibuprofen and paracetamol just from over the counter."
Patient reports taking a medication referred to as "ceraset": "Doctor: Are you on any medication at all? Patient: Just ceraset."

Pollen allergy with hay fever is confirmed: "Do you have any allergies at all..." "Patient: No, I'm just really. Pollen allergy, that's all I have." and "Doctor: Okay, so hay fever? Patient: Yes. Yeah, just hay fever."

Father died of heart attack (myocardial infarction) at 68: "The main one would be heart attack. My. My father passed away of that." and "Doctor: How old is he when that happens? Patient: 68, I think. Yeah."
Work as a nurse is explicitly stated: "Doctor: What do you work as? Patient: I work as a nurse."
Vaccinations up to date including Hep B: "Doctor: And you're up to date with all the vaccinations, Hepatitis B, that kind of thing? Patient: Yes, indeed. Yeah."
Non-smoker status is documented: "Doctor: And are you a smoker at all? Patient: No, I'm not."
Moderate alcohol intake: "Doctor: And do you drink much alcohol? Patient: Moderate alcohol intake? Drink too much." (context implies moderate use).
Moderate exercise a few times per week: "Doctor: And how much kind of physical exercise do you do normally? Patient: I try and do some moderate physical exercise a few times a week."
Fatigue affecting work is described: "I'm really struggling. Quite a lot of work at the moment. It's been quite difficult feeling so tired all the time."

Summary matches transcript: febrile illness for ~7 days with night sweats, myalgias, nausea, and no focal ENT/resp/GI/GU source identified, and unclear etiology. Fever 7 days and systemic symptoms are described, and doctor notes: "there's no apparent reason from what you've told me... if we can't find a focus of infection, then that's something that's an outstanding question that needs to be answered." Patient denied cough/cold/sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, urinary symptoms.

Concern for malaria or exotic infection given travel is explicitly stated: "we need to think about things like malaria or other exotic infections as well" and this is in context of travel to Vietnam with rural exposure 4 weeks ago; prophylaxis details are indeed uncertain as per prior dialogue.

Same-day in-person exam in central London with admin booking and patient to call is described: "we're going to need to bring you into one of our clinics" and "You can come into one of our clinics in central London. That's one option" and "I will send a message to one of our admin team members asking them to book you in, and if you can, ring the number that I leave in your consultation notes after a few minutes and then they'll slot you in." Patient agrees to come in today: "I can come straight into central London today to get that sorted."

Post-exam labs including thick and thin films and inflammatory markers are planned: "and we're going to need to arrange some blood tests as well"; "I'll be asking for something called thick and thin blood films to check for malaria and inflammatory markers and things like that." He states these will be after being seen: "after you've been seen by somebody."

Alternative plan to attend local A&E with notes is given: "if it's inconvenient for you to come into central London because you're living further out, you could actually just attend a local ae... so you could show that to them at reception."
Doctor advises not to work until evaluation completed: "But I don't think you can go into work until we've sorted this out, and we need to sort this out sooner rather than later."
